name: Gelatin tannate
short: Children's trials: adverse events and vomiting not significantly different from placebo; abdominal pain, nausea most common. A review flags tannic acid cell toxicity, few safety data.
text: In a 2020 meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials in children with acute diarrhoea (3 trials, 276 children), adverse events (risk ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.27 to 2.66; two studies; low certainty) and vomiting (risk ratio 1.31, 95% CI 0.95 to 1.80; two studies; moderate certainty) did not differ significantly from placebo; the most common adverse events were abdominal pain and nausea. In an Italian trial in 60 children aged 3 to 72 months given oral rehydration with or without gelatin tannate, no adverse events were reported, and in a placebo-controlled trial in 72 children under 5 in Warsaw, adverse events were a secondary outcome and did not differ between groups (the abstract gives no counts). A 2020 review of products sold in Europe as medical devices rather than medicines, gelatin tannate among them, found that clinical documentation in children was poor, that the leaflets do not mention adverse events or set an age limit, and that the literature raises safety concerns such as cell toxicity of tannic acid and the use of tannic acid doses higher than those established as safe (a review caution, not an observed harm); it adds that some ingredients may affect the absorption of medicines, without naming which. No other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
